New per-job cache selection skips cache operations on darkbloom-* runners without DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL (64–76, 182–194, 312–324, 795–807, 914–926, 1033–1045). Existing branch/event restrictions still prohibit PR cache saves (39). Added restored-.git screening rejects symlinks, active hooks, fsmonitor/hookspath/include configuration and invalid connectivity before checkout (107–132 and repeated blocks). Pinned actions, read-only contents permission and nonpersistent checkout credentials remain visible. No supported security regression was identified in these changes.
Provider native admission, media, lifecycle and prefix gates remain blocking test steps (530–573); prefix-cache disabling here is test-only and does not change T-041 production encryption, account scoping or TTL. Audio fixture caching and nonblocking cluster GPU tests retain their visible controls (574–600, 997–1003). No changed runtime authorization, attestation, prompt encryption, billing or privileged-helper behavior is established by these units (TB-002/TB-007/TB-011, A-001/A-017/A-018).
Integration should verify the newly relied-on Darkbloom cache contract: DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL provenance, actual cache-action endpoint selection, authentication and trusted-branch versus adversarial-PR cache isolation. These implementations are outside the supplied evidence; an attacker-writable trusted cache is not established. Also reconcile provider-plan.yml routing, including the changed GPU lane lookup at 907, with runner isolation and the called build/product actions. Later changed workflow ranges beyond 1051 are not covered by these excerpts. This is local source coverage, not release-artifact qualification or a full audit.
